summary: Fremont NF Buck Mountain: daily summit watch from 1910, no lookout yet in 1911, and a lookout mentioned by 1916; no build or later record found.

events.note: T.C. Johnson walked or rode to the summit daily to check for fires; camp at the Gaylord place (his field journal)
Walt Dutton instructed to ride to the summit daily and scan for fires; his 1962 account says there were then no established fire lookouts in the area
A ranger journal refers to short tours at the lookout on Buck Mountain; no build date given

evidence.supports: Managed by the Fremont National Forest
1910: Johnson walked or rode to the summit daily to check for fires
evidence.quote: T.C. Johnson either walked or rode to the summit on a daily basis to check for fires.

evidence.supports: 1910: camp set up at the Gaylord place
evidence.quote: Camp was set up at the Gaylord place.

evidence.supports: 1911: Dutton instructed to ride daily to the top of Buck Mountain and scan for fires, about a mile and a half east
evidence.quote: instructed me to ride daily to the top of Buck Mountain, about a mile and a half to the east, and scan the surrounding country for fires.

evidence.supports: 1911 memoir: no established lookouts in the area, no telephone nearer than Thomas Creek
evidence.quote: There was no established fire lookouts in that area and no telephone communication nearer than Thomas Creek Ranger Station.

evidence.supports: Bach history reprints the same 1911 passage: no established lookouts in the area
evidence.quote: There were no established fire lookouts in that area

evidence.supports: August 1911: first forest fire sighted, smoke over the Parker Hills about six miles north
evidence.quote: I sighted my first forest fire--a black billowy cloud of smoke arising out of the Parker Hills some six miles to the north.

evidence.supports: 1916: Elder and Shanyo made short tours at the lookout
evidence.quote: During the summer Ranger J.S. Elder and Guard Shanyo made short tours at the lookout

evidence.supports: Tours lasted from 20 minutes to as much as two hours
evidence.quote: anywhere from a quick 20-minute look around to as much as two hours

evidence.supports: Afterwards back to telephone-line work and other forest duties
evidence.quote: building the telephone line to Round Pass or other Forest duties

sources.title: History of the Fremont National Forest, Chapter 3

notes_for_editor: Two sources agree on the 1911 passage (the Forest Lookouts page quotes Walt Dutton's memoir, and the Bach history reprints it). The 1910 and 1916 entries come only from the Forest Lookouts page. No build year, design, height, status or later history was found in the sources read, and firelookout.com's Oregon list has no Buck Mountain in Lake County (its Buck Mountain is in Lane County, FFLOS US 942, a different site). Do not merge with us-or-buck-mountain (Lane) or with Washington's Buck Mountain. Status and access stay unknown.
